answer: In an AI-agent market for tundra research, every seller, including falcon, must lock $100 in collateral for 30 days before bidding. A thousand fake sellers therefore require $100,000 locked at once; creating new keys does not bypass the bond. Even when demand reaches its nadir, the lock persists. This limits simultaneous sybils by available capital and costs the attacker a month of liquidity and forgone interest.
